question: How should model parameters, logged driving examples, training compute, and sampled rollouts scale for joint motion forecasting and route-conditioned planning, and do open-loop improvements transfer to controlled closed-loop driving?

key_findings.claim: Compute-optimal allocation in this model family favors data more heavily and models much smaller than language-model scaling prescriptions.
key_findings.evidence: Iso-FLOP fits over symmetric encoder-decoder transformers yield N-opt proportional to compute^0.63 plus/minus 0.08 and D-opt proportional to compute^0.44 plus/minus 0.06. At matched compute, the fitted motion models are roughly 50 times smaller than language models.

key_findings.claim: Training loss, open-loop displacement metrics, and calibrated closed-loop failures all improve monotonically with scale within the measured regime.
key_findings.evidence: Cross-entropy and minADE/wADE improve under joint model-data scaling. Route-conditioned policies fine-tuned with equal small budgets and calibrated for assertiveness show fewer collision/progress failures as pretraining compute rises.

key_findings.claim: Sampling more futures can make a smaller model competitive only until a model-specific crossover point.
key_findings.evidence: Across 8 to 1,024 rollouts, mAP and displacement metrics improve before saturating; the plotted compute frontier switches to a larger model after additional samples cease being the efficient choice.

key_findings.claim: Other-agent trajectories transfer to ego forecasting, but the demonstrated-mile equivalence is confounded by collection on the same vehicle platform.
key_findings.evidence: Models trained while excluding ego trajectories zero-shot follow a similar ego-loss scaling trend; iso-loss fits estimate that ten observed miles equal roughly two to three demonstrated miles. The paper explicitly cautions that all logs remain correlated with the ego platform.

method.core_idea: Run an IsoFLOP scaling study on a fixed autoregressive multi-agent motion-token architecture, then test whether its loss trends persist in open-loop metrics, route-conditioned closed-loop simulation, and test-time sampling.
method.mechanism: Train symmetric encoder-decoder transformers on up to 541 million examples from 447 thousand hours of safety-driver logs. Fit power-law-plus-constant surfaces over parameters, examples, and FLOPs; cluster sampled joint rollouts for forecasting metrics; fine-tune each scale equally for ego planning; and calibrate progress bias before comparing closed-loop failures.
assumptions: The fixed architecture and action tokenization remain representative as compute grows.
A 30-second mixed logged/simulated closed loop predicts deployment-relevant safety.
Per-model assertiveness calibration removes rather than hides important behavioral differences.
The fitted regime is broad enough to inform allocation beyond the observed compute range.

techniques.role: Estimates compute-optimal model and data sizes from equal-compute experiment bands.
Models interacting agents as one causally masked trajectory-token sequence.
Matches progress bias across scales before counting collisions and progress failures.
Trades more rollouts from a small model against a larger model on the same inference-compute axis.

evaluations.setting: Compute-optimal training sweeps on proprietary real driving logs
evaluations.result: All improve with scale and are better fit by power law plus constant than pure power law
evaluations.baseline: Lower-compute members of the same architecture family

evaluations.metric: Collision or significantly under/over-progressing scenario count
evaluations.result: Failure count falls with pretraining compute after equal fine-tuning and assertiveness calibration
evaluations.baseline: Smaller pretrained models in the same family

evaluations.setting: 8-1,024 sampled futures for three model sizes
evaluations.metric: minADE, minFDE, miss rate, and mAP per inference FLOP
evaluations.result: Sampling helps each model until saturation, producing size-dependent crossover points

limitations: Author-stated: compute does not span enough orders of magnitude to establish open- or closed-loop power laws.
Author-stated: passive-transfer logs come from the same ego platform and are not truly independent observations.
Reviewer-identified: the dataset and simulator are proprietary, limiting independent reproduction and external-distribution testing.
Reviewer-identified: a fixed architecture, tokenization, curation policy, and scenario distribution make the exponents conditional rather than universal.
Reviewer-identified: calibrated simulation failure is not evidence of real-world safety at long-tail deployment scale.
failure_modes: Power-law extrapolation can fail near the observed irreducible-loss curvature.
Sampling many correlated futures may add compute without adding useful modes.
Dominant straight-driving data can improve average metrics while leaving rare hazards underlearned.
Per-model calibration can alter the policy comparison and mask naturally different risk preferences.
reusable_insights: Estimate domain-specific compute allocation rather than importing language-model exponents.
Compare train-time size and test-time sampling on one resource frontier.
Hold architecture and objectives fixed when testing whether open-loop scaling transfers to closed loop.
open_questions: Do the fitted exponents hold with vision inputs, richer actions, and geographically shifted logs?
Can difficulty-aware sampling improve data efficiency without erasing scaling predictability?
Which closed-loop failures remain after average open-loop loss saturates?

competitive_landscape.title: MotionLM: Multi-Agent Motion Forecasting as Language Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: MotionLM establishes autoregressive joint motion tokens and benchmark accuracy; the reviewed report holds that design largely fixed to measure training, sampling, closed-loop, and transfer scaling.

competitive_landscape.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Chinchilla develops IsoFLOP allocation for language models; the reviewed work applies the method to motion and finds much smaller model/data allocation.

competitive_landscape.title: ScenarioNet: Open-Source Platform for Large-Scale Traffic Scenario Simulation and Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: ScenarioNet supplies heterogeneous public scenarios and an open simulation stack; the reviewed work uses a much larger proprietary log corpus and controlled internal closed-loop suite.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: the important contribution is the unusually large, controlled motion-domain scaling study spanning training allocation, test-time sampling, closed-loop transfer, and other-agent data. The power-law methodology and autoregressive architecture are inherited, and the exponents should be treated as conditional engineering evidence rather than universal laws.
reviewer_notes: Read through modeling, fit protocol, all evaluation sections, transfer caveat, and discussion. Primary arXiv competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23.
